about: Made-up chats for the macOS VM screenshots. Every person, project and conversation here is invented; tools/mac-vm/demo_history.py writes them into each agent's own history format. minutesAgo is counted back from the time the history is written, so the chats always look recent.

messages: user
Checkout is timing out for some customers since this morning's deploy. Can you find out why?
assistant

The payment service now retries card authorization three times with a 10 second timeout, so a slow provider holds the checkout request for 30 seconds. The load balancer gives up at 25. I'd cap the retries at one and move the rest to the background queue.
user
Do that, and add a test for the slow provider.
assistant
Done. Authorization retries once inline, and later retries run from the payments queue. The new test simulates a provider that answers after 12 seconds and checks that checkout returns in under 15.
user
Plan the move of the cart service from Redis to Postgres.
assistant

Write to both stores for a week, compare reads in the background and alert on any difference, then switch reads to Postgres and stop the Redis writes. Carts are small, so one table with a JSON column for items is enough.
user
Let's go with the dual-write plan. Start with the schema.
assistant
The carts table has the customer, the items as JSON, and updated_at with an index. The migration is in db/migrations/0042_carts.sql.
user
Should sign-in tokens be stored in local storage or a cookie?
assistant
A cookie marked HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax. Scripts can't read it, so a cross-site scripting bug can't steal the session, and the browser sends it on its own.
user
Decided: we'll use an HttpOnly cookie and drop the local storage token.
assistant
I've moved the session to an HttpOnly cookie, removed the token from local storage, and added a migration that signs old sessions in again once.
user
Invoice exports are stuck in the queue again. Customers with more than 5,000 invoices never get their CSV.
assistant
The export job loads every invoice into memory before writing the file, and the worker is killed at 512 MB. Streaming the rows straight into the CSV keeps memory flat however many invoices there are.
user
Let's stream them. Keep the column order the same so existing spreadsheets don't break.
assistant
Exports now stream in pages of 500 rows with the same columns in the same order. A 40,000-invoice export finished in 18 seconds using 60 MB.
user
How do we round tax on invoices with several line items?
assistant
Right now each line's tax is rounded and then added up, which can be a cent off the total. Most tax authorities expect tax on the invoice total, rounded once.
user
We'll round tax once on the invoice total from now on.
assistant
Tax is now computed on the total and rounded once, half up. Old invoices keep their stored amounts.
user
The release build of the iOS app crashes on launch but the debug build is fine.
assistant
The release configuration strips the analytics module's Objective-C categories, so a selector is missing at launch. Adding -ObjC to Other Linker Flags for the release configuration keeps them.
user
That fixed it, thanks. Can you add a CI step that launches the release build in the simulator?
assistant
Added. CI now builds the release configuration, boots an iPhone 17 simulator, launches the app and fails if it exits within 20 seconds.
user
Search on the docs site doesn't find pages by their old titles after we renamed them.
assistant
The search index only has the current titles. I'd add each page's previous titles as hidden keywords, so old bookmarks and habits still find the page.
user
Good idea, do it for the pages renamed this quarter.
assistant
Added aliases to the twelve renamed pages. Searching for "API keys" now finds "Access tokens" first.
user
Nightly backups are taking six hours now. Why so slow?
assistant
The backup copies every table in full, including the 900 GB events table that only ever gets new rows. Backing up events incrementally by day would bring the nightly run under an hour.
user
Make the events backup incremental and keep weekly full backups.
assistant
Events are now backed up by day, with a full backup every Sunday. Last night's run took 41 minutes.
